notes.setChanged: August 2026 (third pass): the base art was re-authored again and the set cut from six frames to five. The retired frame is ScreenShotAppStore4, the onboarding setup shot - 'Set up in under a minute' was never a reason to install. Shipped order is the array order, not the key number: overdue alert, garage, service history, log sheet, resale value. Frame keys are kept only because the geometry and the render pipeline hang off them.
notes.captionsReplaced: Unlike the earlier re-shoots, this one replaced the caption copy. The new art was authored with its own baked English headlines, and those headlines - not the older calibrated set - are now the source strings; every other locale was retranslated from them. The previous English set ('Know before it's overdue.', 'Every car in one place.', 'Your car's maintenance log.', 'Log a service in 15 seconds.', 'Take your data anywhere.') and its 15 translations are recoverable from git history. Frame 2 now claims 10 seconds, matching the art; the old copy said 15. One string does not match its art: the ScreenShotAppStore6 headline is baked as 'Your Entire Garage in One Place.', which is 31 characters and wraps to three lines in Cambay Bold at 128px in that frame's box. It ships as 'Every Car in One Garage.' instead - same claim, two lines. The baked headline is repainted anyway, so nothing in the image contradicts it.
notes.subtitles: The art's smaller grey subtitle now ships. shipkit's caption pipeline paints a second text run when the spec carries a `type.subtitle` ramp and a frame's copy is `{ headline, subtitle }` rather than a plain string; the headline is fitted first into the band less the subtitle's reserve, and a subtitle that will not fit at its minSize is dropped and reported rather than shipped cramped. The English subtitles are the strings baked into the Figma art; the other fifteen locales are translated from them. The subtitle on ScreenShotAppStore3 is the only place the storefront says 'alerts' rather than showing a list.
notes.captionLevel2026_08_30: ScreenShotAppStore2's caption sat 214px lower than the other three: the baked headline in the raw is what the renderer aligns to, and in that frame the art put it at y=382 against 166/188/168 elsewhere. The band is repainted, not the ink box, so levelling it meant moving the baked ink itself - store/screenshots-raw/en-US/IPHONE_65/ScreenShotAppStore2.png had its band (rows 0-800, already snapped to black) rolled up 214px to ink top 168, and figma-geometry caption.y follows. Nothing below mockTop was touched; max delta outside the band is still 0 for all 16 locales. Three Spanish headlines were shortened in the same pass: es-ES/es-MX ScreenShotAppStore2 ran three lines and, once the block moved up, the third line clamped against the band top, and ScreenShotAppStore3/1 were shrinking to 116-120px. 'Anota un servicio en 10 segundos.' -> 'Un servicio en 10 segundos.', 'No olvides el cambio de aceite.' -> 'Cambia el aceite a tiempo.', 'Historial completo de servicio.' -> 'Historial completo.' - all 16 locales are back to two lines at the full 128px.
notes.casing: English captions follow the art's title case. Other locales use their own sentence case - title case is not a convention in German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese or Swedish, and CJK has no case at all.
notes.lengths: Captions overlay a phone mockup, so each is held near the English source length. `maxLen` per locale is reported below - es-ES/es-MX run longest at 32 and are the ones to re-check for wrapping.
notes.inspectionTerms: Captions deliberately avoid inspection names (MOT/TUV/ITV/vehicle inspection), which differ per market and are already carried by each locale's subtitle.
notes.apostrophe: Captions use the typographic apostrophe U+2019, matching the live art and the store copy. An ASCII "'" renders as a straight vertical tick in Cambay and reads as a typo at 128px.
notes.wrapping: Every locale is 2 lines at the full 128px; no caption is shrunk. Line breaks were tuned by re-rendering, not by character count: the wrap is greedy inside each frame's own box, so ja - which breaks per character, having no spaces - has its comma placed where the break lands (7 characters in frames 1/2/3/6, 8 in frame 5) rather than mid-word.
notes.frameCut2026_08_29: Cut from five frames to four. ScreenShotAppStore5 ("Maximize Resale Value.") showed a product that does not exist: its device art contains a Vehicle Health score, a 100% On-Time Score, Pending Issues, a Verified Digital Logbook and an EXPORT PDF REPORT button. Checked against source - the only export path is src/export/share.ts, which writes text/csv, and none of those strings appear in the i18n catalogue or anywhere in app/ or src/. A health score is also an explicitly rejected product decision: app/onboarding/results.tsx states the results screen is deliberately not a score, because it is a number the app cannot honestly compute. The problem is in the base art, not the localisation - store/screenshots-raw/en-US/IPHONE_65/ScreenShotAppStore5.png is the same screen - so re-rendering the locales would not have fixed it. The raw is kept for the trail and must not be re-staged as it stands. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-29-app-store-screenshot-audit.md. Four screenshots is a complete listing; the remaining four are accurate to the shipped app.

notes.setChanged2026_08_30: Fourth pass, five frames. The garage and log-sheet art were re-authored flat (straight-on) replacing the perspective renders, and a fifth frame was added: ScreenShotAppStore7, the settings screen on a purple glow, headlined '100% Private. Always Yours.' - the privacy claim was previously carried only by the tagline. The oil-change (ScreenShotAppStore3) and service-history (ScreenShotAppStore1) raws are byte-comparable to the third-pass art and were not restaged. Shipped order changed: the log sheet now precedes the service history. New raws were prepped the same way as the third pass - scaled to 1242x2688 (cover, centred), band above mockTop-4 snapped to #000000 keeping only the baked English headline glyphs, baked grey subtitle erased. Band flatness: 0.90 (frame 6), 0.92 (frame 2), 0.85 (frame 7) against the 0.85 gate - frame 7 sits on the gate because its baked headline is the largest ink block in the set.
notes.captionFit2026_08_30b: Three headlines were rewritten to fit the fourth-pass geometry, not for meaning: the log-sheet frame's ink box narrowed from 936px to 843px, which shrank de-DE ('In 10 Sekunden notiert.' at 124px) and pt-BR ('Uma revisão em 10 segundos.' at 116px) below the 128px design size; both were re-cut into shorter lines. The ja privacy headline ran three lines, breaking mid-word ('完全プライベー/ト。'), and was rewritten to '完全に非公開、ずっと自分に。' so the greedy per-character wrap lands on the comma at 7 characters.
notes.jaWrap2026_08_30: The fourth-pass ink boxes changed ja's per-character wrap (frame 6 went 980->1125px, frame 2 936->843px), so three ja headlines were re-cut to break on their comma rather than mid-word: garage 'ガレージ全体、ひとつに。' -> 'ガレージ全体を、ひとつに。', log sheet '整備の記録は、10秒。' -> '整備記録は、10秒。', privacy '完全プライベート。ずっと手元に。' -> '完全に非公開で、ずっと自分に。'.
notes.englishShipsTheArt2026_08_30: en-US, en-GB, en-AU and en-CA ship the unrepainted art: the fourth-pass frames were authored with their English headline and subtitle baked in, so repainting the band only redrew the same words in a different face and position. Those four locale directories are static files, kept byte-identical in store/screenshots-art/IPHONE_65 (scaled to 1242x2688 where the source was not, cover-fit and centred). `ship shots render` with no locale argument WILL overwrite them - render the twelve translated locales explicitly, or restore the four from store/screenshots-art afterwards. The English strings in this file are kept as the source the other twelve locales are translated from, and as the fallback if the English frames ever need to be repainted again.
